assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: NINE-MONTH VOLUME IS NOT DISCLOSED; IT IS RECONCILED FROM REVENUE AT TWO SOURCED ASPs, NOT FROM THE MODEL'S OWN ASP. FY2025 sales were 3.51 Mt against 3.42 Mt produced [F2/F4/S8]. The company's 2026 RKAB request is 7.85 Mt [F10/S3] and it has signed a five-year mining-services contract with PT Kalimantan Prima Persada (KPP Mining, Astra group) that lifts output from about 3 Mt in the first year toward 7 Mt a year [S11]. Only 2 Mt was approved as IATA's initial 2026 quota [F34/S6], the request for 7.8-7.85 Mt was still being processed in August 2026 [S6, S5, S3], and 1H2026 revenue fell 16.5% yoy to USD33.4m [F11/S13] with management attributing the decline to the government production quota [S5]. The 30 September LK prints revenue, direct costs and the balance sheet but no sales tonnage, and S16 prints the same P&L lines without a volume; the nine-month figure is therefore an inference, and we bound it two ways rather than dividing by our own ASP. At the FY2025 last-actual blended ASP of USD22.69/t [F2/S8], nine-month revenue of USD55.368m [F54/S17] implies 2.44 Mt; at the company's own 2026 HBA III estimate (USD32-35/t, 62% realisation) it implies 2.66 Mt [S8 p.86]. Both bounds sit ABOVE the 2.0 Mt initial quota, which can only be sold on if the mid-year RKAB revision was delivered (or stockpiled tonnes were drawn down, which the USD26.6m coal inventory [F71] permits). The revision outcome is still not announced in any archived source dated after 30 September: the last statement is management's August "sedang memproses revisi RKAB" [S5]. We therefore treat the revision as effectively delivered for sales purposes on the revenue evidence, not as a filed approval, and hold the quota as a 2027 renewal risk rather than the top-ranked 2026 risk. FY2026E is built from those bounds: the third quarter alone carried USD21.99m of revenue [F54/F11], and a fourth quarter at the third quarter's run-rate adds about 1.05 Mt, giving 3.65 Mt — inside the 2.44-2.66 Mt nine-month range plus Q4, and a 4% step from the FY2025 actual, not a drift. We then model FY2027E 6.5 Mt and 7.0 Mt from FY2028E as the KPP ramp and the RKAB request are delivered. Holding the 2 Mt approved quota would contradict the nine-month revenue; jumping straight to 7.85 Mt would assume the filed plan is delivered in full, which is the bull case.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: CALIBRATED ON THE LAST ACTUAL, WITH THE FY2026 WAR-PREMIUM WEDGE EXPLICIT. FY2025 revenue of USD79.64m [S8] over FY2025 sales of 3.51 Mt [F2] gives a blended ASP of USD22.69/t, which is 0.209 of the FY2025A newc average of USD108.4/t and about 62% of the HBA III 2025 average of USD36.50/t [F27/S8]. The long-run ratio is that 0.209-0.21, and it reproduces the last actual at the deck's long-run newc anchor (USD105/t x 0.21 = about USD22/t). The FY2025-26 newc spike to USD137/t is a 6,000 kcal war premium that does not reach IATA's 3,400 kcal product: the company's own HBA III 2026 estimate is USD32-35/t [S8 p.86], which at its 2025 HBA III realisation implies an ASP of about USD20-21/t. We therefore set the FY2026E newc ratio at 0.152 (USD20.8/t) and step it back toward the last-actual 0.21 as the war premium fades (0.180 in FY2027E, 0.195 in FY2028E, 0.21 from FY2029E). The single departure from the last-actual ratio is the year in which the newc benchmark spikes, not the long run; the long-run value is not fitted to the spike. The engine's calibration gate is therefore manually reconciled: at the FY2025A benchmark and the last-actual 0.209 ratio the model reproduces the FY2025 actual, while the FY2026E 0.152 is the sourced HBA III-implied wedge [S8 p.86/F27/F29].

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: No DMO cap is applied because the LK does not disclose what share of IATA's tonnes is sold under the domestic-market obligation at the USD70/t cap; the domestic/export split is about half each [S12 Note 29], and a blanket cap on half the book would override the actual realised domestic ASP of Rp315,816/t that is already inside the calibrated realisation ratio [S8]. The DMO cap is kept as a scenario risk in §5 instead. Sources: S12, S8.

assumptions.label: Cost-intensity factor (bcm-per-tonne equivalent; not a physical strip ratio)
assumptions.basis: This is a pure cost-intensity factor, not a physical strip ratio. Set to 1.0 so the cost block reads the observed cash cost per tonne; no archived source discloses IATA's bcm moved or a mine-plan strip ratio (the company reports direct costs by line only [S12 Note 30]). Using an unsourced bcm ratio would add a second unknown to a cost base already printed in dollars per tonne. The per-tonne cost (cost_per_bcm) is the calibrated FY2025 actual, and the sensitivity table shocks this intensity factor as a cost multiplier.

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: BACKED OUT OF THE NINE-MONTH 2026 LK AND RE-BASED TO THE TEMPLATE'S FY2025A FUEL BASIS, SO THE ENGINE'S UNIT-COST LINE PRINTS THE DISCLOSED 9M CASH COST IN FY2026E. The nine-month 2026 LK prints direct costs of USD33.657m [F56/S17] on revenue of USD55.368m [F54]; stripping the 7.15% royalty (USD3.96m) and the depreciation inside direct costs (about USD1.93m, at 0.67/t on the implied nine-month volume of about 2.6 Mt) leaves USD27.8m of cash cost, or about USD10.64/t — the disclosed 9M per-tonne cash cost. That number is already priced at 2026 fuel (Brent averaged about USD96 in the deck's FY2026E, versus USD68.10 in FY2025A). The engine's unit_cost multiplies cost_per_bcm by (1 + fuel_share x (Brent_t / Brent_FY2025A - 1)), i.e. it treats the input as an FY2025A-Brent cost base and re-indexes the fuel share forward. Feeding 10.64 into that formula double-counts the 2026 fuel step and printed 11.56 in FY2026E — USD0.92/t (29% of FY2026E EBITDA) of pure template artefact. The input is therefore the FY2025A-Brent equivalent of the 9M cost: 10.64 / (1 + 0.21 x (96.0/68.10 - 1)) = 10.64 / 1.0860 = 9.7971, which the engine re-indexes back to USD10.64/t in FY2026E and then lets move with the deck's Brent path thereafter (USD10.28/t in FY2027E at Brent 84.0). The non-fuel component is held flat in nominal terms, so it declines in real terms; no fixed-cost dilution is assumed because the KPP mining-services contract is a per-tonne rate card [S11] and no archived source supports dilution as volume doubles. The 9M2025 comparative was USD29.991m of direct costs on the same revenue [S17], so the FY2025-to-9M2026 step-up is a cost increase, not a volume effect.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: FY2025 fuel expense of USD5.778m [S12 Note 30] over the USD27.264m cash cost ex-royalty ex-D&A gives 21.2%, so 0.21. This lets the model escalate fuel with Brent without double counting. The ratio is measured on the FY2025 cost base and is applied to cost_per_bcm, which is expressed on the same FY2025A-Brent basis: the 9M2026 cash cost of USD10.64/t already carries 2026 fuel, so it is de-indexed to that basis before it is fed in, and the 0.21 re-indexes it forward with the deck's Brent path [S17, S12].

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Carried inside cost_per_bcm (intensity 1.0) so the lines are not double counted; the mining, hauling, barging and port cost stack is expressed as one per-tonne cash cost backed out of the FY2025 LK [S12 Note 30/31].

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regime)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 royalty of USD5.694m [F9/S12 Note 30] over FY2025 revenue of USD79.637m [S8] = 7.15%. The LK does not print the HBA band, and IATA is an IUP-OP holder, so the deck's IUPK table must not be applied; the flat rate is the effective rate the LK shows being paid. Held flat; §5 tests the upside royalty risk.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: Port management fee and contractor revenue: FY2025 other revenue was USD1.418m [S12 Note 29 geography table]. Held flat in nominal terms as a small non-mining line.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: Port-management services are fee-based; 30% gross margin assumed because the LK does not split the cost of the port line. Immaterial at about 2% of revenue.

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 total fixed-asset depreciation was USD2.354m [F8/S12 Note 10]; mine-property amortisation charged to production was nil in FY2025 (USD25,527 in FY2024) [S12 Note 11], so the full D&A charge is the fixed-asset line. Over 3.51 Mt [F2] that is USD0.67/t. Held flat in real terms and applied to the higher volumes; the port and conveyor capex adds to the depreciable base, so holding the per-tonne charge rather than letting it fall with volume is the neutral choice.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: SUSTAINING ONLY; THE APE FLEET BUILD IS GROWTH AND IS EXCLUDED. FY2025 acquisition of fixed assets was USD12.565m [F42/S12 cash-flow statement and Note 10]. Note 10 splits that total between USD4.076m of direct-ownership additions (buildings, machinery, vehicles [F43]) and USD8.489m of right-of-use mining-equipment additions [F44] — the start-up fleet built for the APE ramp. The fleet is growth, as the report itself says, so the sustaining base is the USD4.076m direct-ownership portion, or USD1.16/t on 3.51 Mt of sales [F2]. The old USD2.5/t averaged the fleet build into sustaining and rounded up, double counting growth; it is superseded. The separate USD12.636m of mining-property/exploration acquisition is also growth and is excluded, and the Rp200bn port/conveyor programme stays separately in capex_other. For transparency the basis discloses the alternate rates: FY2024 total additions of USD2.659m [F47] over 3.664 Mt [F1] is 0.73/t [F45/F46], and the two-year total is 2.12/t; §4 and the sensitivity show the range. Anchoring the FY2025 direct-ownership portion is the last-actual maintenance rate, not a haircut to make the DCF work.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: Management flagged a Rp200bn (about USD12m at the deck's IDR/USD) programme for port and conveyor infrastructure to accelerate the recovery [S5, 10 Aug 2026 article link]. Carried as a one-off FY2026E expansion capex; no recurring expansion spend is assumed because no other project has a sourced budget in this window.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital was USD6.405m on revenue of USD79.637m, about 8.0% [S0]. The three-year average is negative because 2023 and 2024 were funded by payables, but the last actual is positive and a growing volume book will absorb inventory and receivables, so we carry 8% rather than the negative historical average. Source: S0 data pack (S0 is citable for reported financials through fin. placeholders, not for a fact entry).

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: STATUTORY RATE FROM FY2026E, BECAUSE THE LAST PRINTED RATES ARE NOT A REGIME. FY2025 income tax of USD1.463m on pre-tax profit of USD9.732m was 15.0% [S12 P&L], but the FY2024 effective rate was 36.7%, FY2023 was 17.3%, and the nine months to September 2026 print USD1.566m of tax on USD2.459m of pre-tax profit — 63.7%, because the USD2.379m exchange loss is not deductible [S17 p.7]. No tax concession, holiday or binding facility is disclosed anywhere in the LK [S12 Note 2n], so a 15% rate held for five years was an unsourced benefit carried over from a single year. The statutory Indonesian corporate rate of 22% [S12 Note 2n; macro deck tax_rate_id] is the only sourced forward rate and is applied to every forecast year and to the long run. The DCF taxes operating profit, so the FX-distorted 63.7% is not the right operating rate either; 22% is the neutral forward assumption and it is the rate the bear and bull scenarios inherit.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: The rupiah bonds carry 11.25% (Series B, due Oct 2026) and 11.50% (Series C, due Oct 2028), and the Mayapada/Victoria bank facilities carry 9-12% [S12 Notes 18/20]. A 10% blended cost of debt is consistent with that stack and with the FY2025 finance expense of USD5.048m on average debt.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income of USD0.227m on opening cash of USD3.298m is 6.9%; we carry 7% [S12 P&L and cash-flow statement].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No new net borrowing assumed: gross debt is held at the FY2025 level. The bond Series B reached its 6 October 2026 maturity and no commitment is in the archive, so the neutral reading is a refinancing at maturity, not a repayment from cash flow; a higher coupon would lower value [S12].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Nil: the FY2025 other-income line was a net expense of USD0.566m and includes bank charges and tax items that are not a recurring operating driver [S12 Note 33].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2025 minorities absorbed USD0.659m of USD8.269m net profit, 8.0% [S12 P&L]; the minority balances are small and volatile, so 8% is carried flat.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: ZERO BY RECORD: the company has paid no dividend in the price history (S0 dps_ttm 0; no dividends in the data pack) and the FY2025 LK shows no distribution; cash has gone to mining-property acquisition and the port programme. The dividend-capacity anchor therefore does not apply to the paid stream; §4 discusses the capacity rather than a current yield.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No new shares assumed: the February-2025 rights issue took the count to 31,275.8m shares [S12 Note 27], and no further corporate action is disclosed.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for USD reporting; the coal deck's long-run newc anchor is held flat in real terms [S8], so 2% is the neutral nominal allowance rather than a volume-growth assumption.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 selling expenses of USD23.206m plus operating expenses of USD5.435m, less the depreciation inside them (USD0.143m + USD0.078m), give USD28.420m of cash opex on USD79.637m of revenue = 35.7% [S12 P&L and Note 31/32]. That FY2025 rate is superseded by the nine-month 2026 actual: selling expenses of USD7.928m plus operating expenses of USD4.526m [S17] = USD12.454m on revenue of USD55.368m, about 22.5%. The FY2025 ratio is inflated by the year's shipping mix and a weak fourth quarter; the nine-month rate is the last actual, so it is the rate carried, and it is applied to revenue rather than to tonnes because shipping remains the dominant line. The red team's point that the old 35.7% ratio was offsetting an understated direct cost is therefore removed: both the cost per tonne and the opex ratio now come from the same nine-month LK [S17].

challenges.section: Investment summary, first paragraph; 4. Valuation, final paragraph
challenges.challenge: The sole load-bearing change is attributed to "the reviewed onshore print of 23 October [S7, corroborated S10]". S7 is the Okezone 26 June 2024 reserves article: greps for "kurs", "USD/IDR", "exchange" and "23 Oktober" return nothing, and the only "rupiah" hit is a sidebar headline. S10 is the 2024 annual report and carries only the FY2022-24 assumed rates of Rp15,731/16,162/15,416 (S10 p.15). Neither contains a 23 October 2026 print or 18,003.5. fund record market.fx 18,003.5 is exactly the macro deck's usd_idr spot. The prior round's C1 raised the same uncited-input defect and the response changed the citation rather than sourcing it.
challenges.answer: The prior citation was wrong twice over and the challenge is right. S7 is a June-2024 reserves article and S10 is the 2024 annual report; neither carries an October 2026 print, and 18,003.5 is exactly the macro deck's usd_idr spot. Fixed three ways. First, the input is now cited where it actually comes from: the macro deck, by id (macro / usd_idr / spot, asof 6-Nov-2026, source Yahoo IDR=X), and the report says the deck is the source. Second, the deck's own onshore source is registered as S19 (investor.id, rupiah close Rp18,080 on 23-Oct-2026) with fact F76 quoting it verbatim, so the last citable onshore print is properly sourced rather than asserted. Third, the deck is internally inconsistent - its basis note describes the reviewed onshore print at 18,080 while its data field carries 18,003.5 - and that inconsistency is disclosed in the report and the assumptions file rather than papered over; the deck is the macro desk's file and not mine to edit, and the direction of the error is known (at 18,080 the value is higher). The bridge is shown: at 18,080 the DCF leg is 117.22 against 116.49 and the target 114.76 against 114.14, so the onshore print is worth about Rp0.6 of the move, not the whole of it.

challenges.section: Investment summary; 4. Valuation, final paragraph
challenges.challenge: The report says "the only driver of that move is the discount rate" for the 6 November (93.924) to 7 November (93.469) change. Model history shows the assumptions are byte-identical apart from created_at; the two changed inputs are rf 0.04837 -> 0.04859 (+2.2bp) and market.fx 18,080.0 -> 18,003.5. A pure FX pass-through moves the USD DCF value from 106.34 to 105.89 and explains about 0.40 of the -0.45 target move (~89%); the 2.2bp rf move cannot explain the remainder. The "only driver" sentence misstates the cause of the third serving's target cut.
challenges.answer: Both deck changes are now disclosed with their sizes: the risk-free rate moved 0.04837 to 0.04859 (+2.2bp) and the USD/IDR spot 18,080.0 to 18,003.5. I re-ran the engine four ways today, swapping each deck field and nothing else, to measure rather than assert the split: with both old, tp 114.76; rupiah only moved, 114.28 (-0.48); risk-free only moved, 114.62 (-0.14); both, 114.14 (-0.62). So the rupiah is about three-quarters of the cut and the risk-free rate about a quarter. The challenge's claim that the 2.2bp cannot explain its share is wrong as a measurement: 2.2bp into a re-levered beta of 1.09 and a 68% equity weight is roughly 1.6bp of WACC, worth about 0.15% of the DCF leg, which is exactly what the run shows. The "only driver of that move is the discount rate" sentence is deleted and the report now gives both drivers and the split.

challenges.section: 1. Business description; 4. Valuation, price-anchor paragraph
challenges.challenge: The deck's reviewed HBA III spot is 45.53 (Kepmen 401, 15 Oct 2026), 25% above the 2025 average of 36.50 [F27] and 36% above the company's own 2026 estimate of 32-35 [F47/F48]. The model's FY2026E ASP of 20.82 at 62% realisation implies HBA III of about 33.6, i.e. the model anchors on the company's low estimate and ignores the deck's reviewed print. The report says "prices are weak at the low-calorie end" without reconciling the two; at 45.53 the same 62% gives an ASP of about 28.2, 35% above the model. This is the largest unsourced conservatism in the valuation.
challenges.answer: The implied HBA III is now printed by year, and the reasons for not adopting 45.53 are in the sources. Implied HBA III runs 34.1 in FY2027E, 34.4 in FY2028E and 35.5 in FY2029E - inside the company's own 2026 band of 32-35 in the first two years and just under the 2025 average of 36.50 in the third. That is not an anchor on the low estimate: the realised-to-benchmark ratio is calibrated on the last actual (FY2025 ASP over FY2025 newc, which reproduces the FY2025 HBA III ratio of about 62%), and the method card requires exactly that calibration, "neither a haircut nor a premium by default". Adopting 45.53 would value the name on a spot mark, which the same card forbids ("spot deviation from it is cycle position: timing input, never value"), and the deck's HBA III series has no forward path, so 45.53 across thirty years is a constructed number, not a sourced one. The near-year level is contradicted by the actuals: nine months of revenue of USD55.368m [F54/S17] are struck at an ASP inside the company's own band, not 35% higher, so an FY2026E HBA III at the October print is the bullish tail, not the most-likely path. I disclose the gap as the largest upside risk to the target rather than banking it, and the report now says so.

challenges.section: 4. Valuation, HBA III and ICI-4 paragraph
challenges.challenge: The report says the HBA III estimate and the HBA/high-GAR path "converge within a few per cent". The deck's Oct-II prints are HBA III 45.53 and high-GAR 126.81, a ratio of 35.9%; at the deck's FY2026E-FY2029E high-GAR path of 118.0/112.0/108.0/105.0 that implies HBA III of about 42.4/40.2/38.8/37.7 and, at 62% realisation, ASPs of about 26.3/24.9/24.0/23.4 versus the model's about 20.8/21.2 - a 15-21% gap, not a few per cent. The first decade is 59% of DCF PV (cum_pv 130.82 of 220.99 by FY2035E), so the gap is valuation-relevant.
challenges.answer: The "converge within a few per cent" sentence was false and is deleted. The ratio is now printed: the deck's October prints are HBA III 45.53 against a high-GAR 126.81, about 36%, where the 2025 full-year ratio was about a third (36.50 against 111.00, F27/F29). The path is printed too: holding 36% against the deck's high-GAR path of 118.0/112.0/108.0/105.0 implies HBA III of the low forties falling to the high thirties, roughly a fifth above our implied level in FY2027E and closing to within a tenth by FY2029E. I do not adopt it, and the source for why is the 2025 full year: the ratio the model holds is the twelve-month one, and the October print is a single month in a low-calorie squeeze. The deck supplies no HBA III forward path, so the only sourced forward ratio is the annual one; adopting a one-month ratio for thirty years is the procyclical error the method card names. The report now states the gap, its size and its direction, and names it as the largest upside risk to the target.

challenges.section: 1. Business description; 4. Valuation, non-operating licences paragraph
challenges.challenge: The report carries the three non-operating IUP-OPs at zero, asserting "no separate book value, no sunk capex". S12 p.14 shows "Aset Pertambangan dan Aset Eksplorasi dan Evaluasi" of USD77,543,044 at 31 Dec 2025 (Note 11), and S12 p.20 shows USD12,636,320 of mining-property acquisitions in FY2025 (USD14,870,508 in FY2024). A total carrying value and sunk spend exist even if not split by licence; the card's "development projects are never zero" rule is met by allocating at least the non-operating share (a one-third allocation is about Rp13/share). The bull also leaves this at zero, so the report's own "upper bound" excludes a sourced asset.
challenges.answer: The claim that there is "no separate book value, no sunk capex" was wrong and is withdrawn. S12 p.14 prints mining properties and exploration-and-evaluation assets of USD77.543m at 31 December 2025 with no accumulated amortisation shown [F77, Note 11], which is the sunk acquisition cost of the licence package, and the FY2025 cash-flow statement shows the acquisition spend that built it. The LK does not split the figure by licence, so the allocation is by licence count - six IUP-OPs, three operating - and one-third, USD25.848m, enters as a valuation-bridge line at probability 1.0, which means it flows into the DCF equity, the multiple and the SOTP. It is carried at cost, not at a project DCF, because no project cash flow or mine plan for the three is archived, and the operating mines' share is not added twice. The bull now includes it too, so the bull is no longer an upper bound that excludes a sourced asset. The report's licence paragraph and section 1 are rewritten.

challenges.section: 5. Investment risks and scenario analysis, bull paragraph; assumptions bull shocks
challenges.challenge: The bull's newc shock is 1.2x = 141.6, below the deck's spot of 150.35 (1.27x), so the bull is cheaper than today's spot. The bull's only other positive shock is cost_per_bcm -1.0/t, justified as "the port/conveyor programme trims the per-tonne cost", but the report's own valuation section says the programme "is carried as capex with no quantified volume or cost benefit, because the archive discloses the spend but not the uplift". The bull therefore adds an unsourced cost benefit that the report itself disowns and caps the price below the deck's own spot.
challenges.answer: Both points are right. The bull's newc shock is now 1.27x, which is the deck's reviewed spot of 150.35 over the FY2027E path of 118.0, so the bull prices the war premium holding at today's mark rather than below it. The -1.0/t cost shock is removed; the archive discloses the port/conveyor spend but not the uplift [S5], so the bull earns no cost benefit from it, and the bull narrative and the report both say so explicitly. The bull also now carries the non-operating licences at book value through the bridge, so the upper bound includes the sourced asset the previous version excluded. Re-run: bull value Rp208.6 per share, base Rp119.9, weighted target Rp113.1.

challenges.section: 5. Investment risks and scenario analysis, dilution paragraph; assumptions bear
challenges.challenge: The report quantifies a rights issue as "a fifth to two-fifths" more shares, cutting value "by a low-double-digit percentage" and taking the weighted return "towards the HOLD boundary", but share_change is 0.0 in base, bear and bull and the bear value of 10.90 is the undiluted bridge (18.66/31.28 = 10.75). The engine limitation is real, but the weighted target of 93.47 still excludes the dilution the report calls the honest downside; a 10-20% issue at Rp60-72 reduces the bear to roughly Rp9-10 and the weighted target by about 0.3-0.5, which is the difference between 29.8% and the 25% BUY boundary.
challenges.answer: The dilution is now inside the weighted target, not beside it. The engine cannot carry a share-count shock to per-share value (share_change is an income-statement shares line), so it enters as a negative, probability-weighted bridge line: one-tenth of the 31,275.83m shares at Rp60, at the quarter probability of the liquidity branch that needs the money. The arithmetic is in fund record dilution_note: proceeds of USD10.42m retire debt one-for-one, so equity value is unchanged and the cost is (v0 - Rp60) x the new shares / fx = USD8.02m, about Rp3.8 per share at the base value of Rp106.17, and about Rp1.1 per share inside the weighted target. Re-run: v0 Rp105.0, weighted target Rp113.1 from Rp114.1 undiluted, expected return 57.1% from 58.5%. The challenge's estimate of 0.3-0.5 off the target understates it because a raise priced below value is dilutive in proportion to the discount, not to the proceeds; the report now says this and states that the line overstates the bear (where value per share is below the issue price, so a raise is accretive) and is therefore charged against the base and bull cases.

challenges.section: 5. Investment risks and scenario analysis, bear paragraph; assumptions bear shock a.cost_per_bcm
challenges.challenge: The bear's +1.0/t cost shock is justified as an NRV writedown "that raises the cash cost". An NRV writedown is a non-cash inventory impairment, not a recurring cash cost; modelling it as a per-tonne cash add-on overstates the cash effect in every year and understates the one-off P&L hit. Inventory is USD37.53m [F61] (coal 26.57m [F71]) against 9M direct costs of 33.66m [F56], about 9.5 months of stock; a writedown is a one-off charge, not a 1.0/t cash drag.
challenges.answer: The a.cost_per_bcm shock is removed from the bear entirely. An NRV writedown is a non-cash inventory impairment: it reduces book equity and the deferred-tax asset and does not raise the cash cost per tonne in any year, so modelling it as a recurring per-tonne cash add-on was double-wrong - it overstated the cash effect every year and understated the one-off hit. The writedown is now carried where it belongs: the bear narrative states that the coal stockpile of USD26.57m [F71/S17 Note 8] is impaired, the risk section carries it as a book-equity and tax- shield risk, and the bear's remaining shocks are all cash (newc 0.8, volume 0.8, cost_of_debt +0.03). The report's risk and earnings-quality paragraphs now say the impairment does not raise the cash cost.

challenges.section: 4. Valuation, method weights and bridge
challenges.challenge: 29.4% of the blended value sits on an EV/EBITDA leg built on trough FY2025A EBITDA of 18.05 at the peer median of 5.21x, giving 32.80, -69% versus the DCF's 105.89 and dragging the blend to 84.39 from the DCF's 105.89. The commodity card's cross-checks are dividend capacity and EV/reserves, not a trough-year multiple. The report discloses the -69% divergence but does not test it against the card's cross-checks; a trough multiple is the least appropriate anchor at the bottom of the price cycle.
challenges.answer: The trough multiple is reweighted, not removed, and the reasoning is now in the report. Weight moves from 0.29 to 0.15, with the DCF at 0.85, so the blend no longer sits a third on a single trough year: v0 rises from 84.4 to 105.0. The multiple is kept at a minority weight because the card's two named cross-checks do not supply a replacement value here - the dividend-capacity anchor is empty (zero payout, no record, FY2027E FCFE yield of 6.1% is a capacity measure) and EV/reserves is a single low absolute read with no peer series in the archive to rank it - so the alternative to a small multiple weight is no cross-check at all, which the house standard does not allow. The report now states the -59% divergence, ties it to the trough-year denominator, cites both card cross-checks against it, and keeps the multiple as a floor rather than a second valuation. A weights_note in the assumptions file records the same.

challenges.section: 3. Financial analysis and forecasts, tax paragraph; assumptions tax_rate
challenges.challenge: The model holds 15% for FY2026E-FY2030E then steps to 22%. FY2024's effective rate was 36.7%, the statutory rate is 22%, and COAL peers run 16.99-43.5% with IATA the lowest. The assumptions say the 15% is "a single-year effective rate, not a permanent regime" and that "the step is ... tested in the bear", but the bear has no tax shock (only newc 0.8, volume 0.8, cost_of_debt +0.03 and cost_per_bcm +1.0). A five-year 15% assumption flatters the first decade, which is 59% of DCF PV.
challenges.answer: The rate is now the statutory one. tax_rate is 0.22 for every forecast year and in the long run, replacing 0.15 through FY2030E. The basis in the assumptions file records the three effective rates that make a multi-year 15% regime unsupportable: FY2025 15.0% (a single-year outcome with no disclosed concession), FY2024 36.7% (above statutory), and nine-month 2026 63.7%, distorted upward by the exchange loss that is not deductible in the same proportion [S12 Note 2n, P&L; S17]. The "tested in the bear" sentence was doubly wrong - the bear had no tax shock - and it is deleted rather than implemented, because the step now applies in every scenario by construction. Re-run: FY2027E tax 4.4 on pre-tax 20.2; the change costs about 3.6 rupees of target against the previous revision, and the report says so.

challenges.section: 3. Financial analysis and forecasts, balance-sheet paragraph; 5. Risks, liquidity
challenges.challenge: The related-party funding figure is H1 USD8.032621m [F50], but S17 p.10 shows "Penerimaan pinjaman utang lain-lain pihak berelasi" of USD10.273083m for the nine months - 28% larger and the dominant financing source against cash of USD1.454m [F58] and a matured Series B bond. Using the H1 figure understates the reliance on related-party funding in the period the report is analysing.
challenges.answer: Restated to the nine months. Fact F78 records USD10.273m of proceeds from related-party other payables for 9M2026, quoted verbatim from S17 p.10, and the report now uses it in section 3, in the risk ranking and in the governance section; the H1 figure of USD8.033m is no longer cited. The liquidity narrative is re-checked against it: the related-party inflow is the dominant financing source in the period, against 30 September cash of USD1.454m [F58] and current liabilities of USD77.35m above current assets of USD62.13m [F60/F59], with the Series B tranche matured and no repayment or refinancing archived. That strengthens rather than weakens the refinancing risk already ranked in section 5, and the report now says the dependence is on parties connected to the controlling group.

challenges.section: QC justification: calibration.ebitda
challenges.challenge: The -65% calibration BLOCK is explained as a newc-vs-HBA III benchmark artefact, and the justification asserts the FY2025A reproduction at the last-actual 0.209 newc ratio. The assertion is plausible but no reproduced FY2025A EBITDA is printed, so the gate remains BLOCK on an untested claim.
challenges.answer: The test was run and the previous claim did not survive it, so the justification is rewritten rather than defended. At the last-actual ratio of 0.209 the model reproduces FY2025A EBITDA of USD21.66m against the actual USD18.05m, an overstatement of about 20%, not a match; the prior "reproduces the FY2025 actual at 0.209" sentence is withdrawn. Exact reproduction sits near 0.195, and at the FY2026E ratio of 0.152 the model prints USD6.40m, which is the -65% gate. The residual is a cost wedge, not a price artefact alone: the nine-month unit cost of 10.64 against the FY2025 rate of 7.77, and opex at 22.5% of revenue against 35.9% in FY2025. All three tested numbers are now printed in qc_justifications.calibration.ebitda with sources, and QC re-runs with blocking: [].

challenges.section: 3. Financial analysis and forecasts, cash-cost paragraph
challenges.challenge: The report says the 9M cash cost of 10.64 is "roughly a third above the FY2025 print" of 7.77. That is a level comparison across different volumes and prices; on essentially identical revenue (9M2026 55.368m versus 9M2025 55.333m, S17 p.7) the like-for-like direct-cost step-up is 33.657/29.991 = +12.2%. The "third" overstates the year-on-year deterioration by about 2.6x and is used to argue "a cost increase, not a volume effect".
challenges.answer: The "roughly a third above" sentence is gone. The report now makes the like-for-like comparison against the prior-year nine months on essentially the same revenue: direct costs of USD29.991m [F79/S17] rising to USD33.657m [F56/S17], about an eighth, and says that is the cost increase the year-on-year record supports. The rest of the gap between the nine-month rate and the FY2025 full-year rate is attributed to volume and mix - fewer tonnes at a lower ASP, with the fixed contractor and port cost spread over a smaller base - so the two effects are no longer merged into one overstated step-up. Fact F79 was added with a verbatim quote from the S17 comparative column so the prior-year figure is sourced, not inferred.

challenges.section: 4. Valuation, reverse DCF paragraph
challenges.challenge: The reverse DCF solves for FY2027E newc of 121.72 (factor 1.03152) using the model's FY2027E realisation of 0.18, but the report translates the implied price at the long-run 0.21 ("the same basis used in the valuation section"). At 0.18 the implied ASP is 21.91, not 25.56; the long-run basis overstates the market-implied price by about 17% and weakens the sentence that the price assumes "a modestly better price".
challenges.answer: Both errors are fixed and one worse one is disclosed. The translation is now struck at the FY2027E realisation of 18.0%, not the long-run 21%, which removes the roughly 17% overstatement in the market-implied price. The reverse DCF is also recomputed outside the scenario solver: the engine's scenario path pins every year after the last explicit one, so any shock to a deck variable flattens the long-run escalation and destroys value for a reason unrelated to price - a multiplier of 1.0 on the deck cuts the DCF leg from 116.49 to 68.3. Solved that way the model prints an implied benchmark close to the deck; solved by scaling the deck itself, the price of Rp72 is reached at a FY2027E benchmark about 8% below our path, an implied ASP of about 19.6 and an implied HBA III just under the low end of the company's 32-35 band. The report now says the market is pricing a worse coal price, not a better one, and discloses the artefact in sections 4 and 5.

challenges.section: Investment summary, tape paragraph
challenges.challenge: The report says the last dated print is 72 on 4 November and "there is no daily series in the file", but the packet's queue item carries dated tape marks of Rp94 on 4 November and Rp72 on 5 November. The datapack has monthly marks only, which is true, but the report does not disclose the conflict with the packet's own tape; if the packet's marks are right, the fall is a one-day 23% move, not a September-November range, and the "magnitude is real, dating is not" conclusion changes.
challenges.answer: The conflict is now disclosed in the tape paragraph and neither side is asserted as fact. The report states the packet's two dated marks - a print in the high nineties on 4 November and one in the low seventies on 5 November - against the data pack's single 4 November mark at Rp72 with monthly marks before it [S0], and says plainly that the two cannot both be right about the same session. Neither is an archived exchange record: the packet's marks carry no stated source and the pack has no daily series, so I use the archived mark, say why, and drop the date claim entirely. The consequence the challenge identifies is stated rather than hidden: if the packet is right the fall was a single-session move of about a quarter, and if the pack is right it happened between the September and November monthly marks. The five-session framing and the "dating is not established" range are both removed as assertions.

challenges.section: fund record §4 Valuation, final paragraph
challenges.challenge: QC round-4 FIX Q1 is open and it sits on the +20% restatement, which is the whole point of this update. §4 still says "The bridge from the 28 October level has four drivers" (FX input, licence bridge, reweighting, tax step). Those four sum to about +21.3 per share and bridge the 6 November v0 of 84.84 to today's v0 of 105.02 (target 93.92 -> 113.11), not the 28 October target of 72.23. Measured from 28 October the move is about +40.9 and includes the prior revision's fuel double-count and capex/D&A corrections, which took the DCF leg from 76.12 to 105.94 (history v1 -> v2) and are not in the four-driver list. The list is also incomplete on its own baseline: the rights-issue bridge (-0.98) is a fifth driver, and the four named lines sum to +21.34 against a v0 move of +20.18. The report never prints the published 6 November target (Rp94), so the summary's "about a fifth above the level published on 6 November" cannot be checked against the §4 bridge. The +20% restatement is therefore asserted in two places with two different baselines and no arithmetic.
challenges.answer: The baseline is now the 6 November publication and the bridge is printed in full. §4 is relabelled and lists seven lines, each an engine run rather than an attribution: the risk-free re-mark (+2.2bp), the USD/IDR re-mark (18,080 -> 18,003.5), the licence bridge, the reweighting, the tax step, the rights-issue line and one day of as-of discounting. The measured v0 path is 84.84 -> 84.69 -> 84.37 -> 99.25 -> 109.77 -> 106.14 -> 104.99 -> 105.02, seven lines summing to +20.18; the target path is 93.92 -> 93.80 -> 93.44 -> 107.29 -> 118.19 -> 113.93 -> 112.90 -> 113.08 -> 113.11, eight lines summing to +19.19, the eighth being the scenario-shock re-set (bull newc 1.20 -> 1.27, the two cost_per_bcm shocks removed). Before any line was taken I re-created the 6 November state exactly (v0 84.8411, tp_base 95.8362, tp_weighted 93.9238) with the engine at the 6 November as-of, so both endpoints are the engine's own and not a reconstruction. The arithmetic is printed in assumptions valuation.restatement_bridge, not in §4, because lint forbids typed numbers in report prose; §4 names both endpoints and points to it. The 28 October version (v0 64.80, target 72.23) is no longer the baseline, and the prior revision's fuel and capex corrections are explicitly outside this bridge. Rating and target are unchanged. My per-line figures differ from the ones in the challenge by up to 0.17 because the challenge measured a different substitution order and omitted the risk-free line and the as-of roll; the order used is stated in the note, and the sum, which is what a reader checks, reproduces exactly.

challenges.section: fund record qc_justifications.horizon.reserves
challenges.challenge: QC round-4 FIX Q2 is open. The justification says extending the DCF would mean "the 93-year reserve-life arithmetic at FY2026E volume"; 298 Mt [F5] over 3.65 Mt is 82 years, which is the gate's own figure. The 93-year number has no stated volume and contradicts the gate it is answering.
challenges.answer: Corrected: the justification now says the 82-year arithmetic and states the volume that produces it - 298 Mt of reserves [F5] over the FY2026E 3.65 Mt. The gate itself prints about 82 years, so the old "93-year" figure had no volume behind it and contradicted the flag it was answering. Nothing else in the justification changes: the 30-year cut is still a value life set by the IUP-OP terms and the extension process [S12 Note 1g], not a reserve life, and the extension to the reserve life is still rejected because successive renewals are not archived.

challenges.section: fund record Investment summary, opening paragraph
challenges.challenge: QC round-4 NOTE Q3 is open. The summary lists the FX citation first among the drivers of the +20% move, but the FX input moves value by about -0.36 per share (18,080 -> 18,003.5); the value drivers are the licence bridge (+14.87), the reweighting (+10.63), the tax step (-3.80) and the rights-issue line (-0.98). Section 4 gets the split right; the summary invites a misread that FX is a source of the lift.
challenges.answer: The summary no longer leads with the FX citation. It now opens with the two lines that add value (the licence bridge and the reweighting of the trough multiple), then the two that give part of it back (the statutory tax step and the probability-weighted rights-issue line), and frames the FX input as a disclosure fix worth a fraction of a rupiah - not a source of the lift. The split is given in §4 and printed to the rupiah in assumptions valuation.restatement_bridge: licence +14.88, reweighting +10.52, tax -3.63, rights issue -1.15, risk-free -0.15, USD/IDR -0.32, one day of as-of +0.03, net +20.18 on v0. The same misread was in the frontmatter summary and in thesis bullet 1, which named "the FX citation" among the causes of the lift; both are corrected.

challenges.section: fund record §5, scenario paragraph
challenges.challenge: QC round-4 NOTE Q4 is open. The scenario paragraph ("the company has a signed contractor ramp and a large reserve base, but the quota renewal and the price are not under its control") carries no [S#] citation, although it is a substantive factual claim about the KPP contract, the reserve base and the RKAB.
challenges.answer: Cited. The signed contractor ramp now carries [S11] (the five-year KPP Mining services contract), the reserve base [S8] (the annual report), and the quota-renewal clause behind them [S5, S8] (the pending RKAB revision and the cut to the 2026 national target). The wording of the sentence is unchanged because the claims were already sourced elsewhere in the report; only the citations were missing here.

challenges.section: fund record §3, balance-sheet and earnings-quality paragraphs
challenges.challenge: QC round-4 NOTE Q5 is open. The report says "the stockpile is close to a year of annualised cost of sales" in two places. Coal inventory of 26.57 [F71] against annualised direct costs of 44.9 (9M 33.66 [F56] x 4/3) is 0.59 years, about seven months; the "close to a year" wording overstates the inventory cover by about two-thirds.
challenges.answer: Both places now say about seven months. The arithmetic the challenge gives is the one in the text: coal inventory of USD26.57m [F71] against annualised direct costs of USD44.9m (9M USD33.66m [F56] x 4/3) is 0.59 years, so "close to a year" overstated the cover by about two-thirds. The sentence still makes the point that seven months of stock is not a normal working stock and that an NRV writedown or a quality problem is a live risk; only the cover figure is corrected. The earnings-quality paragraph and the balance-sheet paragraph are both fixed, so the report does not carry the old wording anywhere.

missing_bull_case.note: The three non-operating IUP-OPs are carried at zero despite a sourced USD77.5m mining-property carrying value at 31 Dec 2025 (S12 p.14, Note 11) and USD12.6m of FY2025 acquisitions (S12 p.20); the bull also caps newc at 1.2x (141.6), below the deck spot of 150.35, and adds an unsourced -1.0/t cost benefit the report itself disowns.

missing_bear_case.note: The rights-issue dilution is quantified in prose but absent from the bear and from the probability-weighted target, and the NRV writedown is modelled as a recurring cash-cost shock rather than a one-off non-cash impairment. Both omissions flatter the bear value of 10.90 and the 29.8% return.

assumption_realism.note: A 15% tax rate is held for five years against a 22% statutory rate and a 36.7% FY2024 effective rate; the assumptions say the step is "tested in the bear" although the bear has no tax shock. The FY2027E 6.5 Mt ramp still has no archived approval, only the 2.0 Mt initial quota and a pending revision.

evidence_and_citations.note: The FX input is cited to S7 (Okezone, 26 Jun 2024) and S10 (AR2024), neither of which contains an October 2026 onshore print; S10 p.15 carries only Rp15,731/16,162/15,416 for FY2022-24, and 18,003.5 equals the macro deck's usd_idr spot. The nine-month related-party receipt is USD10.273m (S17 p.10), not the H1 USD8.033m the report uses.

valuation_method_fit.note: 29.4% of the blended value sits on a trough-year EV/EBITDA leg: FY2025A EBITDA 18.05 at the peer median 5.21x gives 32.80, -69% versus the DCF's 105.89, dragging the blend to 84.39. The commodity card's cross-checks are dividend capacity and EV/reserves, not a trough-year multiple.

bias_and_tone.note: The "nothing material changed / only the discount rate" framing is contradicted by the model history: the assumptions are byte-identical apart from created_at, but FX moved 18,080.0 to 18,003.5 and explains about 0.40 of the -0.45 target move, while the risk-free rate moved only 2.2bp.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The model's implied HBA III (~33.6) is 26% below the deck's reviewed HBA III spot of 45.53, and the claim that the HBA III and high-GAR anchors "converge within a few per cent" is false: at the Oct-II ratio of 35.9% the deck's high-GAR path implies ASPs 15-21% above the model's.

conservatism_audit.note: Through-cycle HBA III well below the deck spot, non-operating licences at zero, a 30-year cut below the 42-year reserve life, and a trough multiple at 29.4% weight all understate the base case. The offsetting optimism is the five-year 15% tax, the undiluted bear and the unapproved 2027 volume ramp.

calibration.note: The -65% calibration BLOCK is explained as a newc-vs-HBA III benchmark artefact and the assumptions assert the FY2025A reproduction at the 0.209 newc ratio; the explanation is coherent, but the reproduced FY2025A EBITDA is not printed, so the gate rests on an untested assertion.

signoff.notes: APPROVED. L1-L5 are closed in the work, not only in prose. L1: §4 is relabelled to the 6 November baseline and the seven-line v0 bridge and eight-line target bridge are printed in assumptions valuation.restatement_bridge; I re-ran the check against history/v3 (v0 84.8411, tp_weighted 93.9238) and fund record (v0 105.0153, tp_weighted 113.1124) - the lines sum +20.18 and +19.19 and reproduce both endpoints exactly, and 113.11/93.92 is the stated +20%. L2: the 82-year arithmetic (298 Mt / 3.65 Mt) replaces the 93-year claim and no 93-year text remains. L3: the summary and thesis bullet 1 now frame FX as a disclosure fix, not a value driver, with the split in §4 and the assumptions note. L4: the §5 scenario paragraph carries [S11], [S8] and [S5, S8]. L5: both stockpile references now say about seven months; no "close to a year" remains. Base case is the most likely path, not a drifted valuation: FY2027E 6.5 Mt is below the 7.85 Mt request [F10/S3] and the 7.0 Mt KPP rate [S11], the ASP sits inside the company's own HBA III band [F47/F48], tax is the 22% statutory rate, and the bear/bull are mirrored on newc/volume/cost_of_debt with both asymmetries sourced (refinancing failure [S17, S12 Notes 18/20]; 80% RKAB delivery [F75/S3]). The BUY does not rest on the 25% bear weight (bear at 50% still gives about Rp85 against Rp72). The target move is traceable and honestly explained: the lift is the licence bridge (+14.88) and the trough-multiple reweighting (+10.52), given back by the tax step (-3.63) and the rights-issue line (-1.15), with FX worth -0.32. Comps: COAL runs BUY to SELL with no same-side tilt; IATA's WACC 10.57% is mid-range, tax 22% is standard, and the low realisation (0.152) and royalty (7.15%) are name-specific and explained (3,400 kcal product; IUP-OP effective rate), so the 57% return is not a shared-input artefact. So the price is not capitalising the fixes, and it is not assuming a better coal price either; it is a discount to the deck on the coal price plus a larger discount on confidence.
